verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is scheduled for no earlier than April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'set to launch later today (April 1)'; R4: 'first launch opportunity for Artemis II... is set for 1 April' (page dated 31/03/2026)
verifications.reasoning: Both sources indicate April 1 as the targeted or first opportunity date in 2026 context, matching 'no earlier than'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex... from the launch pad'; R2: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida... Launch Pad 39B'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources directly state the launch is from Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is visible primarily from Florida and parts of Georgia/South Carolina depending on weather.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: 'Skywatchers in Florida and Southern Georgia... Weather permitting... as far afield as... Savannah in southern Georgia'
verifications.reasoning: Supports visibility from Florida and southern Georgia with weather dependence; South Carolina omitted but not contradicted.

verifications.claim: Orlando and Tampa are optimal viewing areas for the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: 'visible... in the nearby city of Orlando... Those in Tampa on the west coast... won't see the rocket until 30-40 seconds'
verifications.reasoning: Specifically mentions Orlando and Tampa as viewing locations with timings, but does not describe them as 'optimal'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is visible to the naked eye for about 70 seconds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'Artemis 2 will be lost from view just 70 seconds after launch'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states visibility duration of 70 seconds to the naked eye.

verifications.claim: The Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex offers ticketed packages for close-up views of the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'guests with an Artemis II Launch Viewing Package... two launch viewing packages... Main Visitor Complex Launch Viewing Package... Feel the Heat Launch Viewing Package'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly describes ticketed packages for launch viewing from the Visitor Complex at close distances.

verifications.claim: Many beaches and roads in the Space Coast region provide vantage points for the Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention beaches, roads, or Space Coast vantage points.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch can be watched on NASA’s YouTube channel.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention NASA's YouTube channel for viewing.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch can be watched on the ESA website.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'Watch the Artemis II launch live here... Tune in... on ESA Web TV'
verifications.reasoning: Directly provides live viewing on ESA site/Web TV.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is most likely visible across Florida.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: 'Skywatchers in Florida... Orlando... Tampa on the west coast... Jacksonville to the north'
verifications.reasoning: Mentions visibility across multiple Florida locations spanning the state, but not explicitly 'across Florida' or 'most likely'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch has potential sightings further north including parts of Georgia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'Florida and Southern Georgia... glimpsed from as far afield as the city of Savannah in southern Georgia'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports potential visibility further north in parts of Georgia.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch can happen at any time of day or night.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'the launch could occur any day, at any time of day or night'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing confirms flexibility in launch timing.

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II launch the rocket is expected to appear in the east.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: 'The SLS rocket should become visible in the east for skywatchers in the nearby city of Orlando'
verifications.reasoning: Specifies appearance in the east for Orlando viewers, but claim is general; no broader confirmation.

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II launch the rocket is expected to move rapidly away from the launch pad.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'see the rocket leave the launch pad... clears the tree line'; R3: 'ascended to an altitude of over 40,000 feet (12,190 meters) on its journey to low-Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Implies rapid movement away via ascent descriptions, but 'rapidly' not explicitly stated.
